historical_references.reference: Santram was a renowned Jain monk and scholar during the Gupta Empire in the 4th to 6th centuries CE. He is credited with composing the 'Santram Suri Prakasha', a Jain text that elucidates the Jain monastic rules and rituals.

Another reference to Santram can be found in the 'Prabandha Chintamani' by the Jain scholar Hemachandra (1089-1173 CE). Hemachandra mentions Santram as a great Jain ascetic and scholar who is revered for his profound knowledge and spiritual practices.
